title: Decide class finiteness by paid closure search versus strict ancestor pumping
statement: Dovetail two finite effective searches on the monotone population transition system: breadth-first reachable closure until no new enabled successor exists, and finite reachable paths containing an ancestor a and descendant b with a<=b componentwise and a!=b. The first halts on a finite reachable set. Such a comparable pair in the second search pumps the intervening reaction word from b,b+(b-a),... by monotone translated enabling, proving infinitely many reachable states. If the reachable set is infinite, its finitely branching BFS tree is infinite; Konig yields an infinite branch of distinct populations and Dickson gives such a strictly different comparable pair. Exactly one side therefore eventually certifies finite or infinite. Every transition, population encoding and explored path is paid; total termination gives a complete-input computable BIT bound, with no polynomial/optimal-complexity claim. This decides finiteness, not the positive gap of an infinite class.
